proof.text:
Put $T(i,j)=t_i\cdots t_{j-1}:K_j\to K_i$ for $j\ge i$, with $T(i,i)=1$, and $P=\prod_{i\ge1}K_i$, $P_e=\prod_{n\ge1}K_{en}$, $D=1-s$ and $D_e=1-s_e$. In the reordered, signed coordinates $(x,y)=(x_{\rm cone},-y_{\rm cone})$, the stipulated shifted cone has terms $P^q\oplus P^{q-1}$ and differential $d_R(x,y)=(dx,Dx-dy)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The identity $T(i,j)T(j,k)=T(i,k)$ is the tower composition law [def-weil-inverse-system]. Hence finite cancellation gives
$$ (b_eDx)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}\bigl(T(en,i)x_i-T(en,i+1)x_{i+1}\bigr)=x_{en}-T(en,e(n+1))x_{e(n+1)}=(D_ea_ex)_n. $$
Both $a_e$ and $b_e$ commute with internal differentials, since every $T(i,j)$ does. Thus $r_e(x,y)=(a_ex,b_ey)$ is precisely the induced chain map of the two cones.

proof.text: Construct a section of this particular map. For each $i\ge1$, let $m(i)$ be the least positive multiple of $e$ with $m(i)\ge i$. Define $\alpha:P_e\to P$ by $(\alpha u)_i=T(i,m(i))u_{m(i)/e}$, and $\beta:P_e\to P$ by $(\beta v)_{en}=v_n$, with all other coordinates zero. These are maps of internal complexes. Directly $a_e\alpha=1$ and $b_e\beta=1$. If $i$ is not a multiple of $e$, $m(i)=m(i+1)$, so $(D\alpha u)_i=0$. At $i=en$ it equals $u_n-T(en,e(n+1))u_{n+1}$. Therefore $D\alpha=\beta D_e$, and $j(u,v)=(\alpha u,\beta v)$ is a chain map with $r_ej=1$. This also treats the initial indices $1\le i<e$: they are extended backward from $e$, rather than discarded.

proof.text:
Let $U=\ker a_e\subset P$ and $V=\ker b_e\subset P$, computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The square from Step 1 restricts $D$ to $D_U:U\to V$. For $y\in V$, define $c(y)_{en}=0$. At a nonretained index $i$, let $m=m(i)>i$ and put
$$ c(y)_i=\sum_{k=i}^{m-1}T(i,k)y_k. $$
These are finite sums of sheaf morphisms and define a map $c:V\to U$ of internal complexes. At a nonretained index, cancellation gives $(Dc(y))_i=y_i$. At $en$, the equation $(b_ey)_n=0$ gives $y_{en}=-\sum_{k=en+1}^{e(n+1)-1}T(en,k)y_k=-t_{en}c(y)_{en+1}$, so the same equality holds there. Conversely, telescoping $\sum_{k=i}^{m-1}T(i,k)(Dx)_k=x_i-T(i,m)x_m=x_i$ for $x\in U$ gives $cD_U=1$; retained coordinates are zero on both sides. Thus $D_Uc=1$ and $cD_U=1$. No surjectivity of any transition is used.

proof.text:
In the coordinates of Step 1 the kernel $E=\ker r_e$ is $E^q=U^q\oplus V^{q-1}$ with differential $(u,v)\mapsto(du,D_Uu-dv)$. The degree $-1$ map $h(u,v)=(cv,0)$ satisfies
$$ d_Eh(u,v)+hd_E(u,v)=(dcv,v)+(u-cdv,0)=(u,v). $$
The equality uses $dc=cd$ from Step 3. Since $r_ej=1$, the chain map $L=1-jr_e$ takes values in $E$. With $\iota:E\to R$ its inclusion, the degree $-1$ map $H=\iota hL$ therefore satisfies $d_RH+Hd_R=1-jr_e$. On a cycle $z$, this says $z-jr_ez=d_RHz$, a boundary. Thus $jr_e$ induces the identity on $\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$, and $r_ej=1$ does as well on the other complex. Consequently every $H^q(r_e)$ has inverse $H^q(j)$, proving the required quasi-isomorphism by the definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All formulas are identities of sheaf morphisms; no passage from presheaf cohomology to sheaf cohomology is used.

proof.text:
For a tower map $f_i:K_i\to K'_i$, induction on $j-i$ in the transition equation gives $f_iT(i,j)=T'(i,j)f_j$. Substitution into the formulas for $a_e,b_e$ proves naturality of $r_e$. For successive restrictions by $e$ and $f$, the first-coordinate map is $a_fa_e=a_{ef}$. On the second coordinate, the block sum for the restricted tower is
$$ \sum_{n=fk}^{f(k+1)-1}T(efk,en)\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T(en,i)y_i=\sum_{i=efk}^{ef(k+1)-1}T(efk,i)y_i. $$
Thus $b_f^{(e)}b_e=b_{ef}$ and the actual cone maps compose strictly, with $r_1=1$. For a strictly compatible augmentation $\gamma:P_0\to K_\bullet$, $D(\gamma_i)_i=0$, so its cone map is $p\mapsto((\gamma_i p)_i,0)$. Applying $r_e$ gives $p\mapsto((\gamma_{en}p)_n,0)$, exactly the restricted augmentation.

proof.text:
Here and below $-\otimes_AB$ means $-\otimes_{\underline A}\underline B$ for the constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Choose a finite $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$, with dual maps $\lambda_a:B\to A$. For any module sheaf $M$, the mutually inverse maps
$$ M\otimes_AB\longrightarrow M^r,\quad m\otimes b\longmapsto(\lambda_a(b)m)_a,\qquad (m_a)_a\longmapsto\sum_a m_a\otimes b_a $$
are defined using the sectionwise tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and then sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The identities follow from $b=\sum_a\lambda_a(b)b_a$; on arbitrary sections of $\underline B$ this identity follows by sheafifying the corresponding identity on the constant presheaf. For any family $M_i$, the canonical map
$$ \gamma:(\prod_iM_i)\otimes_AB\to\prod_i(M_i\otimes_AB) $$
then becomes the rearrangement $(\prod_iM_i)^r\to\prod_i M_i^r$, $(m_{i,a})\mapsto(m_{i,a})$. Its inverse sends a family with basis coordinates $m_{i,a}$ to $\sum_{a=1}^r(m_{i,a})_i\otimes b_a$. This is a finite sum, so it defines a sheaf morphism for any countable family and on any site. The canonical map $\gamma$ is consequently an isomorphism; the basis proves invertibility without entering its definition.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; finite-basis calculation using algebra.tex Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product

proof.text:
The map $\gamma$ is natural and $B$-linear: on local tensor generators it is $(m_i)_i\otimes b\mapsto(m_i\otimes b)_i$, so $\gamma(zb')=\gamma(z)b'$ and it commutes with every componentwise module map. The same finite-basis rearrangement identifies $(M\oplus N)\otimes_AB$ with $(M\otimes_AB)\oplus(N\otimes_AB)$ and commutes with negatives. Applied in every degree, these maps therefore give a chain isomorphism
$$ \theta:\mathsf R(K_\bullet)\otimes_AB\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf R(K_\bullet\otimes_AB). $$
Indeed $\gamma(sx\otimes b)=(t_ix_{i+1}\otimes b)_i=s_B\gamma(x\otimes b)$, and the internal differential and the signed cone differential are preserved term by term. Finally $a_e(x)_n=x_{en}$ is preserved by tensoring, and
$$ \Bigl(\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T(en,i)y_i\Bigr)\otimes b=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}(T(en,i)\otimes1)(y_i\otimes b). $$
Thus $\theta$ commutes with $r_e$ on both cone coordinates. On an augmentation $(\gamma_i p,0)$ it gives $(\gamma_i p\otimes b,0)$, its scalar extension. These equalities on local tensor generators give sheaf morphism equalities by the defining sheafification; they also prove naturality of $\theta$.

title: Cofinal restriction of a Roos tower complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a commutative ring, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A)$ the category of sheaves of modules over its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact. Let $K_\bullet$ be a strict tower of cochain complexes with chain maps $t_i:K_{i+1}\to K_i$, $i\geq1$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Write $\mathsf R(K_\bullet)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_iK_i\to\prod_iK_i)[-1]$, where $(sx)_i=t_ix_{i+1}$; products are termwise and for $f:X\to Y$ the cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^q=Y^q\oplus X^{q+1}$ with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(d_Yy+f(x),-d_Xx)$. For an integer $e\geq1$ let $K^{(e)}_n=K_{en}$ with transition $t_{en}\cdots t_{e(n+1)-1}$. The maps between the two product arrows given by
$$a_e(x)_n=x_{en},\qquad b_e(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}t_{en}\cdots t_{i-1}y_i$$
(empty products are identities) induce a natural quasi-isomorphism $r_e:\mathsf R(K_\bullet)\to\mathsf R(K^{(e)}_\bullet)$. These maps commute with composition of restrictions to subsequences and send a strictly compatible augmentation $P\to K_\bullet$, represented by its product map and zero shifted-product component, to its restricted augmentation. For a finite free commutative $A$-algebra $B$ placed in degree zero, the canonical tensor/product maps give a natural isomorphism
$$\mathsf R(K_\bullet)\otimes_A B\cong\mathsf R(K_\bullet\otimes_A B)$$
which is $B$-linear, commutes with every $r_e$, and carries the augmentation maps to their scalar extensions. All these assertions use the specified maps on complexes, before passing to the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
